castra, castrōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

a camp; barracks

Other words

  • mīlitum contubernium — barracks

    also used · modern · Traupman 185; Traupman 277

    Classically contubernium is the sharing of a tent, or the squad that shares one (Lewis & Short); Traupman widens it to the soldiers’ quarters. A permanent camp was castra statīva (Lewis & Short s.v. statīvus).

See also camp, comrade, army, soldier.

SourcesLewis & Short: contubernium · Lewis & Short: stativus
